prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” AI video ad maker — the right one depends on what you need (talking-head avatar ads, short social clips, large-scale localized campaigns, creative generative visuals, budget, integrations). Below are best-in-class options by use case and what they’re best at, plus how to choose.

My context: my detailed knowledge goes up through mid‑2024, so names and capabilities below reflect that timeframe and the major tools and trends that were strong then. If you want, tell me your exact goals/platforms/budget and I’ll give a tailored short list and one recommended tool.

Best options by use case

- Talking‑head / spokesperson AI (realistic avatars for product/service ads)
  - Synthesia — very polished AI presenters, good language support and enterprise features. Great for professional-looking talking-head ads without actors.
  - HeyGen (Movio/Elai class tools) — similar to Synthesia, sometimes cheaper; good for quick multilingual ads.
  - Elai.io / Colossyan — other alternatives with avatar options.
  - When to pick: you want on‑camera presenters, script → video, multiple languages/voices.

- Short social ads / automated repurposing (quick vertical/horizontal clips)
  - Pictory — converts long form text/audio to short clips, good auto-highlights and subtitles.
  - Veed.io — easy editing, auto-subtitles, templates for social ads.
  - Opus Clip / Clipchamp / InVideo / FlexClip — fast templates and exports in ad aspect ratios.
  - When to pick: you need many short variants for Instagram, TikTok, Reels, or YouTube Shorts.

- Creative / generative visuals & advanced editing
  - Runway — strong generative video tools and advanced editing with AI removal/replacement tools.
  - Kaiber / Gen-1 competitors — experimental generative visuals for attention-getting creative ads.
  - When to pick: you need eye-catching, novel visuals or heavy creative iteration.

- Scale, testing & localization for performance ads
  - VidMob, Shakr, Promo.com — focus on ad template systems, many variants, and creative analytics. Good for agencies/brands running many variants and A/B tests.
  - When to pick: you run many campaigns across countries and need automation + analytics.

- Budget / all-in-one template makers
  - Canva (video templates + AI features), InVideo, Promo, Lumen5 — inexpensive, easy to use, good template libraries.
  - When to pick: small business or single-owner creating ads quickly with low cost.

How to choose (questions to ask yourself)
- Output format: vertical (TikTok/Instagram Reels) vs horizontal (YouTube). Does the tool export all needed aspect ratios?
- Volume: one-off ad vs hundreds of localized variants.
- Style: live presenter, animated text, stock footage montage, or novel generative visuals?
- Languages & voice: do you need native-sounding voiceovers or translated scripts?
- Integrations: do you need direct integration with Facebook/Google Ads, asset libraries, or analytics?
- Budget: free tier/trial? subscription vs per-video pricing?
- Legal/brand concerns: rights to avatars, stock footage, and use of synthetic likenesses.

Quick pros/cons and pricing notes (general)
- Synthesia / HeyGen: pros — great avatars and languages; cons — cost per video or per minute; possible brand/consent issues for real-person likenesses.
- Pictory / Veed / InVideo: pros — low learning curve, fast templates; cons — less realistic avatars/limited generative novelty.
- Runway: pros — cutting-edge generative tools; cons — steeper learning curve, heavier compute cost.
- VidMob / Shakr: pros — enterprise-grade production + optimization; cons — pricier, better suited for scale.

Safety & legal
- Check license terms for stock content and avatars.
- If using synthetic human likenesses, ensure rights/consent and consider platform ad policies (some platforms restrict certain synthetic content).

If you want a single recommendation right now
- If you want talking‑head product/service ads: try Synthesia (or HeyGen if you want a lower-cost alternative).
- If you want to produce lots of short social ads quickly and cheaply: start with Pictory or Veed (or Canva if you want broad design features).
- If you want creative, attention‑grabbing visuals: test Runway for a few concept ads.

Want help picking one? Tell me:
- Platform(s) (TikTok, Meta, YouTube, TV)
- Ad style (talking head, product demo, montage, animated)
- Volume (single ad vs 50+ variants)
- Budget per month or per video

I’ll shortlist 2–3 tools and suggest a quick workflow and estimated costs.
